answer: A registry that charges a refundable stake in timber-backed credits for each agent identity makes Sybil attacks expensive: creating a thousand fake agents on a dune of sand costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents earn theirs back through verified work. Each identity must also publish a unique sonnet-length proof of useful computation, so duplicates are detected and their stakes slashed. Attackers then face real capital loss per fake identity, while legitimate newcomers pay only a temporary deposit.
